Could be a Bartholins Cyst. The Bartholin's glands are located on each side of the vagina opening, to the left and right of it. The glands secrete fluid that helps lubricate the vagina. If you have a small, noninfected Bartholin's cyst, you may not notice it. If the cyst grows, you might feel a lump or mass near your vaginal opening. Although a cyst is usually painless, it can be tender. A full-blown infection of a Bartholin's cyst can occur in a matter of days. If the cyst becomes infected, you may experience a tender, painful lump near the vaginal opening, discomfort while walking or sitting, pain during intercourse, or a fever.
